children: Artificial-intelligence spending is set to enter a new phase in 2027, with growth remaining explosive even as investors brace for a slowdown beyond the peak years, J.P. Morgan says in a report. The bank predicts global AI capital expenditure will nearly double to $1.4 trillion in 2027, driven by hyperscaler data-center expansion and surging demand for GPUs. The report estimates 151 gigawatts of new AI data-center capacity will be added between 2027 and 2031 at a cost of roughly $7 trillion, although power constraints, financing limits and growing political scrutiny could temper growth after 2027. AI infrastructure investment is increasingly shifting toward silicon, with GPU-related spending expected to approach $1 trillion annually by 2031, it adds. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
